handoff.summary: Generalized private IntegerBuffer authority from one named buffer to an authenticated state-layout manifest derived from the complete fused H1 call graph. The static audit classifies all 348 root IntegerBuffers as 328 written private candidates, 20 public/read-only buffers, and zero rejected, with authenticated inventory and candidate hashes. Generated storage uses a root-local 1024-slot pointer table, preserves the ordinary clearing path for unregistered or revoked owners, and canonicalizes all dirty private owners exactly once at root success/failure publication. The full 100,275,455-byte target was inspected without compiling; focused tests prove manifest mutations, raw access, aliases, returns, unknown calls, and fallback fail closed.
risks: Global no-clear violates the public canonical IntegerBuffer ABI and must not be restored.
Only five candidates have prior cleared-word counters; 323 candidate contributions remain unmeasured.
The 328-buffer layout has passed static and focused tests but not a bounded fused native replay.
Broader raw-buffer cross-backend qualification remains required before enabling private authority beyond authenticated private roots.
next_steps: Run one authorized 600-second/4-GiB fused H1 build and exact profile with all 328 candidates, requiring every frozen relation, compact-owner, RNG, root, and getfu hash/counter plus canonical public buffers.
Retain the full layout only if the bounded replay is exact and improves the declared phase threshold; otherwise record the rejected hypothesis without weakening public ABI semantics.
